result.summary: Independently re-verified REQ-025 (scheduled job runner + idempotent send-once notification ledger, GitHub issue #28, depends_on REQ-024, first requirement of Phase 5) at commit 08da742, branch feature/WF02-REQ-025. Did not trust TEST-RUNNER's Step 4 report or requirement_status.yaml history as a substitute for my own re-derivation. 1. Read docs/agents/design/REQ-025.md and REQ-025-schema.md in full against all 6 ACs. Confirmed the shipped code matches the design line-for-line: apps/bot/src/domain/notification.ts's sendLedgeredNotification() implements §3.1's 5-step rule table exactly (user lookup -> unconditional blocked check -> classification-gated broadcastOptIn check -> the single atomic ledger INSERT with 23505 caught as skipped-already-sent -> compose+send, never rolled back on failure); handlers/withdraw.ts's sendPromotionNotification is the thin composeMessage+one-call rewrite §4 describes, keyed on the promoted (not withdrawn) registration id; scheduler/rateLimiter.ts and scheduler/runner.ts match §5/§7; index.ts wires startScheduledJobs([]) with one process-wide createRateLimitedSender instance passed to the withdraw handler, exactly as §7 specifies. 2. Read handoffs/WF02-REQ-025/step-04-test-runner.json and test-reports/report-2026-09-07-WF02-REQ-025.yaml, then re-ran everything myself rather than accepting them. 3. Re-ran npm run lint myself: 0 errors, 2 pre-existing apps/web LCP warnings (Footer.tsx, Nav.tsx), unrelated to this diff -- matches the report. Re-ran npm run build myself: apps/web (Next.js/Turbopack) and apps/bot (tsc) both clean. Stood up my own scratch Postgres (apps/bot/docker-compose.yml, port 55432), ran npx drizzle-kit migrate myself (applied cleanly, migration 0005_violet_venom.sql only), then npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism from the repo root: 20 files / 228 tests passed, 0 failed -- matches the report's count exactly. 4. Independent re-verification, using my own fresh fixtures/harnesses (apps/bot/rv-p1.ts, rv-p2.ts, rv-concurrent.ts, written fresh, never reusing BACKEND-DEV's or TEST-RUNNER's scratch scripts or notification.test.ts's fixtures), all deleted after use: - AC1 genuine two-process kill-then-restart: p1 (npx tsx) built a fresh fixture (chapter/venue/published event capacity 5, a real registerForEvent call), called sendLedgeredNotification(kind='reminder_24h', classification='transactional') with the kill point constructed as `.then(() => process.exit(0))` strictly after send() resolved. p1 exited 0. Direct SQL before p2: exactly 1 notification_ledger row, delivery-log exactly 1 line (pid 27332). p2 (a separate npx tsx invocation, fresh Pool/drizzle instance) read the registrationId from a sidecar file and called the identical sendLedgeredNotification: outcome was exactly {"kind":"skipped-already-sent"}. After p2: delivery-log still exactly 1 line (same pid as p1's -- sender.send never called again), ledger count still exactly 1. PASS, independently reproduced. - AC2 direct duplicate-insert against the table itself (no in-memory record): first INSERT (registration_id, kind='admission_result') succeeded; an identical second INSERT failed with Postgres 23505 naming uq_notification_ledger_registration_kind; a third INSERT with the same registration_id but a different kind ('feedback_request') succeeded, confirming genuine compositeness. git grep -nE 'new (Set|Map)\s*<|new (Set|Map)\s*\(' across notification.ts/rateLimiter.ts/runner.ts/withdraw.ts: zero matches. PASS. - Concurrent-call race, separate-pool granularity, my own fixture: two independent Pool/drizzle instances both called sendLedgeredNotification for the SAME (registrationId, kind='event_cancelled') concurrently via Promise.all. Result: exactly one 'sent', one 'skipped-already-sent', exactly one sender.send() call recorded across both. PASS. - REQ-023 promotion path through the new ledger-backed mechanism, end-to-end: ran the real, existing 'REQ-023 AC6' vitest case (real bot.handleUpdate dispatch through withdraw:confirm callback, not a direct domain call) against my own migrated scratch Postgres -- 1 passed. Queried notification_ledger directly afterward: exactly 1 row with kind='waitlist_promotion', confirming the promotion notification genuinely flows through sendLedgeredNotification end-to-end, not a bare ctx.api.sendMessage call. - AC3/AC4/AC5/AC6: spot-read the code directly (step 1 above) rather than re-running the full vitest matrix a second time, since the full-suite run in step 3 already re-executed these cases live; confirmed SendNotificationInput.classification has no '?' and no default (AC5, notification.ts line 37), the broadcastOptIn check is gated strictly behind classification==='marketing' (AC3, step 3), and the blocked check precedes it unconditionally (AC4, step 2). 5. Confirmed full requirement scope: git diff master...HEAD --stat lists exactly the design-doc-listed files (schema.ts, one new migration + its meta files, domain/notification.ts + its test file, domain/user.ts's broadcastOptIn addition, handlers/withdraw.ts's rewrite + test tweaks, scheduler/rateLimiter.ts, scheduler/runner.ts, index.ts's wiring, the two design docs, the test spec, ISS-0022, and this run's own handoffs/test-report) -- nothing stray. git grep for TODO/FIXME/XXX across the 6 changed source files: zero matches. git status --porcelain clean before this handoff (all scratch scripts and the scratch Postgres container+volume torn down). 6. Filed-issue judgment: ISS-0013 (MAJOR, no CI Postgres service) and ISS-0020 (MAJOR, REQ-018 staff.ts blocked-user gap) both pre-date this run and are explicitly out of scope -- ISS-0020 is the design's own §0.1 scope decision (staff.ts's (event_id,user_id)-keyed sends structurally don't fit this ledger's (registration_id,kind) key, and S9 doesn't even apply to staff.ts's synchronous request-scoped sends). ISS-0013 is a standing CI-infrastructure gap unrelated to this requirement's own correctness (I compensated for it here exactly as TEST-RUNNER did, by standing up and migrating a scratch Postgres myself). ISS-0014 through ISS-0019, ISS-0021, ISS-0022 are all MINOR test-spec/test-infrastructure wording precision issues (grep-count nits, fixture UUID typos, an ALTER-TABLE wording gap that doesn't affect the actual zero-existing-tables-altered property). None of these touch the shipped code's actual correctness. Judgment: none of the filed issues should block this release. 7. Foundation-solidity assessment (explicitly asked for): S9 (idempotency) rests entirely on a real Postgres UNIQUE constraint with no in-memory component anywhere -- independently reproduced via both a genuine two-process kill test and a same-process concurrent race, at the DB layer directly via duplicate insert. S10 (classification) rests on a two-branch, no-default TypeScript union enforced structurally at the one call site. Both are exercised for real by REQ-023's live promotion path today, not just by synthetic reminder_24h stand-ins. REQ-026/027 can build directly on sendLedgeredNotification, NotificationKind, and startScheduledJobs with no gap I could find. Overall: every independent check -- lint, build, the full 228-test suite from the repo root, my own two-process AC1 kill test, my own AC2 duplicate-insert, my own separate-pool concurrent race, and a live re-run of the real REQ-023 promotion path with a direct ledger-row check -- agrees with all prior gates (CODE-DESIGNER/VALIDATOR, DATA-DESIGNER, BACKEND-DEV, REVIEWER, SECURITY-REVIEWER, TEST-DESIGNER/VALIDATOR, TEST-RUNNER). No half-implemented scope, no stray TODOs, clean git tree, all design-doc-listed files present.

issues.description: Carried forward and independently re-confirmed: ISS-0022 (REQ-025 test-spec's AC-schema wording, 'no ALTER TABLE whatsoever', doesn't account for drizzle-kit's standard FK-constraint ALTER TABLE on a new table's own foreign key). The actual property the spec exists to protect (zero existing tables' columns altered) holds -- confirmed directly by reading the migration file. No action needed for this release; recommend TEST-DESIGNER tighten the wording on a future spec revision.
